body.html: Aramis Hotel is a 3-star city-center hotel in Nakhon Sawan, on Sawanvithi Road in the Pak Nam Pho district of Mueang Nakhon Sawan. Open since around 2012, it is a property of roughly 69 rooms that locals and business travellers know well, set in the central Pak Nam Pho area within walking distance of the market and city restaurants. Most guests who choose it are people in town for business and meetings, travellers who want a central base that is easy to explore on foot, and drivers stopping over on the way north, since Nakhon Sawan is an important waypoint.

Rooms come in several types, from Superior at around 28 sqm to Deluxe and Deluxe Corner at about 33 sqm. The detail reviews mention most is how spacious and clean the rooms are, decorated in a simple, modern style, with comfortable beds. All rooms have air conditioning, a TV, a fridge and a private bathroom with a water heater. The praise you see most often is that rooms feel larger than expected for the price, cleanliness is good, and staff are friendly. The thing to accept is that some bathrooms have no shower screen, so the floor gets slippery when wet and water can run onto the bedroom floor — worth keeping in mind.
"Spacious, clean rooms, comfortable beds, helpful staff, plenty of parking, a central location you can walk to the Pak Nam Pho market from, a decent breakfast, and good value for the price."

The facilities are well-rounded for this class of hotel. There is an on-site restaurant, a buffet breakfast, ample free parking, free Wi-Fi, a lift, EV charging and a 24-hour front desk. There is a minimart and some shuttle service too, which is handy for travellers. What many guests single out is the generous parking that is easy to find a space in — rare for a city-center hotel. One thing to note is that there is a small swimming pool that some reviews describe as small and not very private, and a few items may carry an extra charge, such as a pillow rental fee, so it is worth asking first.

Location is the hotel's strong point. It is in central Pak Nam Pho, about 600 metres from Sawan Park (Nong Sombuon), near Nakhon Sawan Church, and within walking distance of the Pak Nam Pho market and city eateries. It is around 6–7 kilometres from Nakhon Sawan Railway Station and sits in a spot that is easy to drive in and out of, making it good for a stopover or for business in town. The overall score sits around 8.3 from real reviews, with platforms praising the spacious rooms, cleanliness and central location, while the points it loses come from noise on higher floors and some bathroom details.

To be straight with you, Aramis Hotel is a city-center hotel that sells spacious, clean rooms, plenty of parking and the Pak Nam Pho location at a good price, not a luxury property with every facility. If you expect a large pool or a resort atmosphere, it may not be for you, and some higher-floor rooms can pick up street noise, lift noise or pigeons. But if you see it as a central Nakhon Sawan stay with spacious, clean rooms, a breakfast, easy parking, and the market and restaurants on foot, all at an affordable starting price, it stands out for value and location among Pak Nam Pho's city-center hotels.

Tips from reading through the reviews: ask for a mid-level floor or a room away from the street if you are sensitive to noise, since some higher-floor rooms catch street noise and pigeons. Choose a Deluxe or Deluxe Corner if you want a roomier, more comfortable stay. Confirm any extra charges, such as pillow rental or breakfast, before checking in. Having your own car is convenient thanks to the generous parking. In the evening, walk out to the Pak Nam Pho market and nearby riverside eateries for plenty of good local food. And always compare the live price on Agoda and Booking before you book, as rates shift with the season and promotions.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Aramis Hotel Nakhon Sawan

faq.q: Where is Aramis Hotel and what is nearby?
faq.a: It is at 288/20 Sawanvithi Road, Pak Nam Pho, Mueang Nakhon Sawan, in the heart of the Pak Nam Pho district. It is about 600 metres from Sawan Park (Nong Sombuon), near Nakhon Sawan Church, and within walking distance of the Pak Nam Pho market and city eateries. It is about 6–7 kilometres from Nakhon Sawan Railway Station, making it ideal for staying central or for a stopover.

faq.q: How much does Aramis Hotel cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about ฿1,000/night for a Superior. There are also Deluxe King rooms from around ฿1,100, Deluxe Twin from around ฿1,200 and Deluxe Corner from around ฿1,400. Rooms run from about 28 to 33 sqm. Rates move with the season and promotions, so always compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Aramis Hotel best for?
faq.a: It is best for people in town for business and meetings, travellers who want a central, walkable base, and drivers stopping over on the way north who want spacious, clean rooms, a breakfast and convenient parking at an affordable starting price. It suits those who value roomy accommodation and location over resort-style facilities.

faq.q: Does Aramis Hotel have breakfast and what facilities are there?
faq.a: Yes — there is an on-site restaurant, a buffet breakfast, ample free parking, free Wi-Fi, a lift, EV charging and a 24-hour front desk. There is a minimart and some shuttle service too. There is a small swimming pool, though some reviews say it is small and not very private. A few items may carry an extra charge, such as a pillow rental fee, so it is worth asking first.

faq.q: What are the rooms at Aramis Hotel like?
faq.a: Rooms split into Superior (around 28 sqm) and Deluxe/Deluxe Corner (around 33 sqm). What reviews agree on is that the rooms are spacious and clean, with simple modern decor and comfortable beds. They have air conditioning, a TV, a fridge and a private bathroom with a water heater. Note that some bathrooms have no shower screen and the floor gets slippery when wet, and some higher-floor rooms can pick up noise.

faq.q: Are the review scores for Aramis Hotel reliable?
faq.a: The overall score sits around 8.3 from real reviews across platforms, with Booking around 8.4 and Agoda around 8.3. On TripAdvisor it has 4 out of 5 stars and ranks #5 of 17 hotels in Nakhon Sawan. The strengths reviewers agree on are the spacious rooms, cleanliness and central location, while the points it loses come from noise on higher floors and some bathroom details.
